prompt:
Agents can't do anything with households yet: Spoonjoy's actions and MCP tools have nothing for them. Add the agent side. The households service already has createHousehold, listHouseholds, getHousehold, renameHousehold, createInvite, emailInvite, previewInvite, acceptInvite, revokeInvite, changeMemberRole, removeFromHousehold and leave (app/domains/households-and-identity). Plan the actions: their ids, inputs, outputs, consent, and the descriptions agents read.

Reply with your answer in this chat; don't change any files.

events.message: I'll look at the service and the existing declarations first.

arguments.command: cd app/domains/households-and-identity && ls -R . | head -50; ls ../../../actions; grep -rn "export.*function\|export const" --include=*.ts -r . | grep -i "household\|invite" | head -40
arguments.description: Inspect households domain and actions folder

arguments.command: sed -n 1,260p app/domains/households-and-identity/application/households.server.ts; sed -n 1,40p app/domains/households-and-identity/model/invite.ts; sed -n 95,125p actions/access.mts; grep -n "consequential\|consent" tools/ouro-actions/ouro-actions.mts | head -20; grep -rn "scope" actions/*.mts | head -8; cat actions/fields.mts | head -30
arguments.description: Read service, invite model, consent levels, scopes

arguments.command: sed -n 22,40p tools/ouro-actions/ouro-actions.mts; sed -n 55,104p app/domains/households-and-identity/model/household.ts; sed -n 38,75p app/domains/households-and-identity/model/invite.ts; grep -n "scope" app/lib/mcp/*.ts | head -15
arguments.description: Read consent doc, role rules, invite validation, MCP scopes

events.message:
# Plan: agent actions for households

I changed no files. This is based on `households.server.ts`, the household and invite models, `actions/shopping.mts`, `actions/access.mts` and the consent classes in `tools/ouro-actions`.

**Layout.** Add `actions/households.mts` and add its array to `spoonjoy.actions.mts`. Then run `pnpm actions:generate`. Each action gets an operation in `spoonjoy-api.server.ts` that spreads `declaredOperation("<id>")` and calls the service through `d1HouseholdStore`. The declared-actions unit test must pass. Add a `households` MCP scope that is not part of the default agent grant, and update the `start_agent_connection` text ("kitchen and shopping-list scopes only"). All field labels and descriptions are in plain language. Shared fields are `householdId` ("from list_households"), `memberId`, `inviteId` and `ownerEmail` (protocol-only).

**Consent classes**

| id | consent | input | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_households` | read | – | `[{id, name, role, memberCount}]` |
| `get_household` | read | `householdId` | `{id, name, me, members[{userId, username, role}], invites[{id, role, usesLeft, email, expiresAt, status}]}`. Only an owner sees invites. A missing or non-member household returns "not found". |
| `preview_invite` | read | `token` | `{householdName, role, status}` |
| `create_household` | write | `name` (≤80), `idempotencyKey` | `{id, name}`. It's the caller's own space, and they become its owner. |
| `rename_household` | write, idempotent | `householdId`, `name` | `{id, name}`. Owner only. |
| `leave_household` | consequential | `householdId` | `{}`. The last person to leave deletes the household. |
| `accept_invite` | consequential | `token` | `{householdId, joined}`. It starts sharing the caller's household-visible recipes with others. |
| `create_invite` | consequential | `householdId`, `role` (member or viewer), `uses` (1–50), `days` (1–30), optional `email` | `{inviteId, role, expiresAt, joinUrl}` |
| `email_invite` | consequential | the same, with `email` required | `{to}` |
| `revoke_invite` | consequential, idempotent | `householdId`, `inviteId` | `{}` |
| `change_member_role` | consequential | `householdId`, `memberId`, `role` | `{}`. Owner only; you can't change your own role. |
| `remove_from_household` | consequential | `householdId`, `memberId` | `{}`. Owner only; you can't remove yourself or another owner. |

Consequential means an agent prepares the action and the person confirms it.

**Decisions to confirm**
- **Invite link secret.** `create_invite` returns the join URL (the token) once, since only its hash is stored. Descriptions must say to show it to the person and not to send it anywhere itself. Treat it like the API token secret, and never log or echo it in telemetry.
- **Email invite.** If mail fails, the service turns the invite off again. Surface this as a typed "unavailable" error that points to `create_invite`.
- **Open question.** Should `accept_invite` and `create_household` be person-only? I propose consequential and write respectively, matching the "agent prepares, person says yes" model. Making them person-only is a one-word change if you want it stricter.
- **Errors.** Map `forbidden` to a permission error and `unavailable` to a service error. Pass the service's own wording through, because it is already agent-readable ("Make someone else an owner before you leave.").
- **Ownership.** Always use the signed-in caller as `userId`. The `ownerEmail` field is only for a local server with no signed-in person.

**Agent descriptions (draft, one per action)**
- `list_households`: "List the households the person belongs to, with their role in each."
- `get_household`: "Open one household: its members and roles. An owner also sees its invites, with how many uses are left and when they expire."
- `create_household`: "Make a household the person owns, to share lists and meal plans with others."
- `rename_household`: "Rename a household. Only an owner can."
- `create_invite`: "Make a join link for a household. Roles are member or viewer only; an owner promotes someone after they join. The link is returned once: show it to the person, don't send it yourself."
- `email_invite`: "Email an invite to one address. Only the Spoonjoy account with that email can use it. Needs the person's go-ahead before it sends."
- `preview_invite`: "See which household an invite link joins, with its role and whether it still works, before accepting."
- `accept_invite`: "Join the household an invite link is for. Someone already in it is let through without using the invite up."
- `revoke_invite`: "Turn off a household invite. Only an owner can."
- `change_member_role`: "Change a household member's role to owner, member or viewer. Only an owner can, and not for themselves."
- `remove_from_household`: "Remove a member. Only an owner can, and not an owner (change their role first). To remove yourself, use leave_household."
- `leave_household`: "Leave a household. An only owner must name another owner first. The last person to leave deletes the household."

**Tests.** Add unit tests per operation for the success, forbidden, validation and unavailable paths, and check that MCP annotations match the consent class. Also update docs (`docs/api.md` and `docs/claude-connector.md`) and `claims-urls.json` if a new claim is cited. Journeys aren't needed unless a web control is added.

criteria.evidence: The plan is organized by the service's functions. Its table lists one action per service function (list_households, get_household, create_household, rename_household, create_invite, email_invite, preview_invite, accept_invite, revoke_invite, change_member_role, remove_from_household, leave_household). It never frames the work as agent jobs such as 'who is in mine' or 'invite someone'.

It mirrors the service one action per function. It keeps `create_invite` and `email_invite` as separate actions instead of merging them into one invite job. It leaves nothing out and gives no reason why any action earns its place.

Inputs and outputs are small and use shared fields (`householdId` ("from list_households"), `memberId`, `inviteId`). Consent is assigned with reasons ("It's the caller's own space" for write; consequential for actions that affect others). Failures say what happened and what to do next: "Surface this as a typed 'unavailable' error that points to `create_invite`" and "Pass the service's own wording through... ('Make someone else an owner before you leave.')".

The only proof planned is "unit tests per operation for the success, forbidden, validation and unavailable paths, and check that MCP annotations match the consent class." It says "Journeys aren't needed" and never has fresh agents do a household job through the actions.

verdict.summary: The answer carefully details consent, inputs, outputs and errors, but it mirrors the service function list one action at a time and plans no proof by fresh agents.
